messages:
ashley (Support): heads up — customer Maya reported intermittent 401s after we rotated their SSO-linked API key this morning. they see errors from some worker pods but not all. repro steps attached below.

maya (Customer): we rotated the key via the console at 08:12 UTC, then started getting 401s around 08:18 on ~20% of requests. some requests immediately succeed, others fail with 401 until we restart the pod. seems nondeterministic.

ashley (Support): thanks @maya. can you confirm whether you're on Dedicated or Hosted?

maya (Customer): Dedicated pool in eu-west-1, using our private deployment. sidecar-based secret injector.

ashley (Support): copying SRE + DevEx — @jake @kevin — likely related to sidecar/env propagation but want to capture logs first.

jake (SRE): curious — is the sidecar using an in-memory cache that keeps old token until restart? we've seen this with the old envproc sidecar where kube env var refresh wasn't atomic. any logs from the sidecar?

maya (Customer): attaching snippet.

maya (Customer): ```
2026-03-14T08:18:23Z sidecar-abc123 INFO fetched secret key=redacted lease=abcd1234 ttl=3600
2026-03-14T08:18:25Z app-1 ERROR request failed status=401 endpoint=/v1/generate token=sha1:oldkey...
2026-03-14T08:18:26Z sidecar-abc123 INFO background refresh succeeded key=redacted lease=efgh5678
2026-03-14T08:18:27Z app-1 INFO request succeeded status=200
```

ashley (Support): this pattern matches a propagation race — app kept using old token between first request and background refresh.

kevin (DevEx): pinging infra: do we have any recent changes to the env var hot-reload behavior? maybe we introduced delayed file symlink swap.

ops-bot: deploy event: service/private-sidecar v3.4.1 rolled out at 07:50 UTC to eu-west-1

deploy-bot: deploy started by @infra-release at 07:48 UTC — affected pods restarted in waves until 07:56 UTC

jake (SRE): notable: deploy completed shortly before rotation, so some pods got new sidecar image while others still running previous. if there were behavioral changes, that could explain partial failures.

kevin (DevEx): can we reproduce locally? maya — do you have a quick repro we can run? a curl that returns 401 vs 200?

maya (Customer): yes — they run this in a loop against a single pod:

maya (Customer): ```bash
for i in {1..10}; do \
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" https://private.example.com/v1/generate; \
  sleep 1; \
done
```

maya (Customer): using rotated key value for $API_KEY. sometimes the first few iterations show 401, then flip to 200 without restarting pod.

jake (SRE): run that against sidecar logs, looks like: the app reads token from env at process start, but sidecar updates file on disk asynchronously. if the app keeps token only in memory, it won't pick up the new value until restart — unless there is an agent to reload. I want to check the injector pattern: are we writing secret to env var or to a file that the app sources?

maya (Customer): sidecar writes to /etc/secrets/apikey and sets env var `API_KEY_FILE=/etc/secrets/apikey` and the app reads at start and caches. we pushed a small hot-reload earlier but maybe not on this deployment.

kevin (DevEx): ok — two vectors: (A) the sidecar race between rotate and file update, (B) stale in-process caches. Both produce intermittent 401s and explain the restart mitigation.

ashley (Support): mitigation suggested to customer: restart the affected pods to force refresh (short-term). longer-term options below.

jake (SRE): quick checks I ran on the cluster:
```
# check vault leases for customer namespace
kubectl exec -n customer-ns vault-sidecar-xxx -- vault lease list | grep customer-audit
# check sidecar rollout age
kubectl get pods -n customer-ns -o wide | grep sidecar
```
I also found the sidecar log across pods shows small timing skew ~10–20s between file write and app detection.

kevin (DevEx): can we patch the sidecar to write a temp file and then move atomically (mv) so inotify sees a single replace? or update the injector to notify the app via SIGHUP?

jake (SRE): atomic move would help — currently we write directly which causes inotify races depending on FS. However the real issue is the app caches the token in-memory instead of reloading on file change. we should push guidance: apps should either read token from file per-request or subscribe to file-change events.

ashley (Support): filing escalation ticket to track root cause and customer comms. draft message: "We've identified a propagation race between the secret injector sidecar and in-process caching. Restarting the pod forces the new key to be used; we're rolling a patch and will provide a permanent fix." any additions?

kevin (DevEx): add that this is more likely when rotation happens right after a multi-wave deploy. recommend an automated propagation grace window (delay rotation signal until all sidecars in pool report updated lease).

jake (SRE): agree. also record affected pods and ask customer for logs for each pod IP. include command to collect quick logs:
```bash
kubectl logs -n customer-ns pod/<pod-name> -c app --since=1h > pod_app.log
kubectl logs -n customer-ns pod/<pod-name> -c sidecar --since=1h > pod_sidecar.log
```

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0412 assigned to infra-team — visible in incidents channel

kevin (DevEx): temporary workaround script we can offer to customer to rotate with a small drain:
```bash
# rotate-key-with-drain.sh
kubectl label ns customer-ns rotating=true
kubectl rollout restart deployment --namespace=customer-ns --selector=app=worker --timeout=5m
# run rotation in keymanager API now
# unset label
kubectl label ns customer-ns rotating- || true
```

maya (Customer): thanks. we'll do restart for now — can you patch the injector? we prefer not to run drain script ourselves.

jake (SRE): I'll open a PR for the sidecar atomic write + optional SIGHUP notification. low risk change. will target canary in eu-west-1 tomorrow.

kevin (DevEx): I'll draft a KB article: "API key rotation and sidecar propagation best practices" that recommends an orchestration pattern, examples, and a grace window.

ashley (Support): next steps: 1) ask maya to restart affected pods (done) 2) SRE to push sidecar atomic write PR and canary (jake) 3) DevEx to publish KB and rotation script (kevin) 4) Support to follow up customer and close when stable (ashley). I'll update incident with links + timeline. cc @ops-bot @deploy-bot. :white_check_mark:

maya (Customer): restarted pods, testing now — will report in an hour. thanks everyone!

jake (SRE): note for postmortem: consider making rotation operation idempotent and cluster-aware (wait-for-ready across all pods) and surface a propagation status in rotation API. avoids thrusting new key before all consumers are ready.

kevin (DevEx): also log the rotation event with a correlation id customer-side so we can match 401 spikes to rotation activities in the future.

ashley (Support): closing loop: I'll follow up after maya confirms. keeping this open until we have sidecar PR and KB published.

maya (Customer): FYI — after restarts things look stable so far, no more 401s in 30m. will reopen if it recurs.

ops-bot: incident INC-2026-0412 status updated: monitoring -> mitigated

sso-bot: audit event: api_key.rotate user=maya@example.com at 08:12 UTC id=rot-9f3a

ashley (Support): thanks all. saved notes to the ticket. :pray:
